Definition: probably of foreign origin; a hillock:--hill.
BiblicalUsage: A hill is a hillock, a rise in the ground — and it appears twice, in a promise and in a warning. In Luke 3:5 Isaiah's word is quoted: every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low. In Luke 23:30 Jesus says, then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us, and to the hills, Cover us.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the hills in Luke are the two ends of the story: brought low when the way is prepared, and called on for cover when the judgment comes.
